title: G9 fix round 1: pick_executor falls back to weight times score when no measured executor clears the floor, and the success floor is computed per task class (review T-0304)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain 8a84cfa "route executors by local expected cost" (T-0275) in git log; never drop it.
Review T-0304 on T-0275: (high) pool.pick_executor returns None (task held) when every measured executor sits below [models].success_floor instead of falling back to the weight x score ranking its docstring and the README promise; reproduced with two executors at success 0.2 and scores luna 5.0, terra 1.0. (med) the floor uses the executor's global merged/failed record, not the record for the task's class, although pool.toml documents it as a per-class gate.
Change:
1. pool.pick_executor: candidates with an expected cost and a per-class success rate at or above the floor are ranked by expected cost; if that set is empty, rank every enabled in-range executor by weight x score exactly as before G9 (never return None while any enabled in-range executor exists).
2. scorecard: per-class success rate = merged / (merged + failed) over that executor's tasks of the class (task_class() applied to each task with run rows), exposed as scorecard.class_success(executor_id, task_class); pick_executor uses it; pool.toml comment for success_floor states it is per class and requires min_samples of that class.
3. Tests: tests/test_pool.py::test_pick_falls_back_when_all_below_floor (the reviewer's scenario picks luna), tests/test_scorecard.py::test_class_success_is_per_class (good overall, poor in security: security below floor, mechanical above); keep the five T-0275 tests green.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows 8a84cfa below your commit
tests/test_pool.py::test_pick_falls_back_when_all_below_floor passes; tests/test_scorecard.py::test_class_success_is_per_class passes; the five T-0275 tests still pass
pool.toml comment on success_floor says per class
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree
